doc.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Playing music the audience can digest: storytelling
summary: Music should offer melodies listeners can take home; scales and chords are only tools and the point is storytelling.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well said. I like the term, the audience could digest. Something that is acceptable to them and they can get something out of.

Yeah in other words they could take home something. I remember he really played, because he played a nursery rhyme over here. You know? I mean they would relate to something. A melody here that they can pick up on. Not a bunch of scales and chords. Those are just elements of creation. I mean those are just tools of creation. Sort of like using all the crayons in the Crayon box, or all the tools in the toolbox. You know? You

just use — but anyway it all about storytelling. All about storytelling, just like I’m talking now. I’m telling the story and I’m trying to make it as interesting as possible. I’m trying to articulate ideas that people can relate to, instead of using a lot of academic phrases that — the music is over their head.
Yeah. That doesn’t work. Of course I had to learn that but it’s like something that I’ve learned just putting this music together I have to do the same thing with interviews and conversation.
